props.text: Scenarios bias the simulation. Every alarm you see still goes through the normal Ignition alarm pipeline - evaluation, deadband, delay, priority and journal.
Plant runs healthy. Alarms clear and the rate settles.
Catchment runoff. Raw turbidity spikes, filters load up, pH drops - a cascade across three areas in about a minute.
Residual decays to a Critical compliance breach. The alarm your customer actually cares about.
An intake pump and a high lift pump trip together. Watch the standby pick up and network pressure hold.
Head loss climbs, then turbidity breaks through - High then Critical, in the right order.
High Lift Pump 3 flaps. Use it to demonstrate finding and shelving a bad actor.
The jam blocks everything upstream, the line stops, and OEE starts falling. Downtime you can watch accumulate.
Chilled water climbs, batch temperature follows it up through High and on to a Critical food-safety limit.
Receiver drains, pneumatics fail, the whole line stops - one utility fault taking out four areas.
Carbonation drifts and fill rejects climb. A quality alarm rather than a breakdown.
Straight to the Critical quarantine alarm.
The Diagnostic-priority case, so the priority scale is not just theory.
